statement: Manifest schema v2 installations preserve v1 compatibility while requiring every normalized artifact export to declare a unique name, a stable interface type, and explicit exact table read/write sets; the default scaffold emits v2 and SQL INSTALL SERVICE persists those declarations through the existing immutable service package catalog.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

EXTEND src/service/external-service-manifest.js and the existing ServiceLifecycleCommandOwner -> ServiceInstallCatalogOwner -> service_packages.normalized_manifest path. Do not add an artifact registry, package table, lifecycle ingress, or validation owner.

Manifest schema v1 remains accepted with its existing normalized meaning. Schema v2 becomes the scaffold default and is the only version in this Quest that carries analyzable export access declarations; both versions normalize through the same manifest owner.

Every v2 export has a unique name, a non-empty stable interface identifier, and explicit reads/writes arrays containing sorted unique exact lowercase table:<schema>.<table> references. Wildcards, implicit sets, duplicate names, and unknown export fields are rejected.

This Quest does not define the seven binding source schemas, source-to-interface compatibility, a binding table, cell reconciliation, context placement, or artifact execution. Those remain downstream concerns.

The deterministic scenario must prove the real SQL INSTALL SERVICE owner path persists the canonical v2 export declarations in service_packages.normalized_manifest, while malformed v2 input is rejected before artifact resolution or catalog mutation and the generated service scaffold emits valid v2 declarations.

Proof covers the manifest owner, generated scaffold, SQL lifecycle consumer, immutable catalog tail, v1 compatibility, deterministic order normalization, negative schema attacks, static owner guards, and red-on-revert engagement.
